widgets_values: A cozy corner bookshop at dusk, warm amber light spilling from the windows onto wet cobblestones. A hand-lettered chalkboard sign stands by the door, reading "OPEN LATE" in clean capitals. Rain-speckled glass reflects soft neon from across the street. Photorealistic, 35mm, shallow depth of field with the sign in sharp focus, rich cinematic color grading, subtle film grain.

## AMD Qwen Image 2.1 Text to Image

Requires an account key. Register at https://h3.oneclickamd.ai, then configure it either way below. **One-time setup per machine** — it applies to every workflow:

- Save the key to `h3_gateway_api_key.txt` in the ComfyUI user directory
- Or set the environment variable `H3_GATEWAY_API_KEY`

The same key also works for the AMD MiniMax H3 video nodes, so configure it once.

**On the Windows Desktop app, use the file.** Desktop starts from the Start menu and does not inherit variables you set in PowerShell. It belongs in Desktop's install directory, for example `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Comfy-Desktop\ComfyUI-Installs\ComfyUI\ComfyUI\user\h3_gateway_api_key.txt`. Make it with Notepad: the default encoding is right, and **New > Text Document** already ends in `.txt`.

If the key is missing, the node fails immediately and tells you the registration URL and the exact file path, so you never sit through a silent 401.

**Your key is not in this workflow.** The node has no `api_key` widget, so the key is never written into the workflow JSON or embedded into exported image metadata. This workflow is safe to share.

If you run your own gateway, override the default address with `H3_GATEWAY_BASE_URL`.

**Parameters:** `aspect_ratio` six ratios; `model` picks between `Qwen-Image-2.1` and `Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo`. Turbo costs the same and is about twice as fast, and runs at a step count the gateway pins, so the `steps` slider only appears for the base model. A 1024x1024 image takes about 23 seconds on the base model and 13 on Turbo.
